What Dada PSA is

Everyone

Dada PSA is where every IT request at PMC lives. It has two doors: PMC Requests for the people who ask, and the desk for Dada IT.

PMC RequestsFor every staff member, at help.pmcne.ph or through the Employee Portal. You see only your own requests.
The deskFor Dada IT, at desk.pmcne.ph, signed in with Microsoft. Every request lands on a board with a number, a priority and running clocks.

Never write a patient's details. Not in a request, a note, an email reply, an article or a file name. The ward, the room and the machine are all Dada IT ever needs.

  1. It arrives from PMC Requests, an email, a phone call or a monitoring system.
  2. It lands on a board with a number, a status, a contact and a priority from two plain questions.
  3. The clocks start: Respond, Resolution plan, Resolve.
  4. Someone owns it, writes notes, books a visit if needed, records time.
  5. It is resolved and closed, and the requester is asked how we did.

Asking for help

Follow, add to and approve requests

Ward staffApprovers
  • Add a note or photo, or reply to the email keeping the reference in the subject.
  • Emails never carry the details.
  • Approvals come to your department's approver under Approvals; a decline must say why.

Working the desk

On your phone

Technicians

Nothing to install. Open the desk in your phone's browser: the board becomes cards, and a ticket has Note, Ticket and Call at your thumb.

Your day

Schedule, Dispatch and In / out

TechniciansManagers

Schedule is the week by person. Dispatch is today. In / out is the board by the door.

  • Book a visit from the ticket's Schedule card or under the week; the desk warns of a double booking.
  • Time off, a meeting or an activity goes in the same week.
  • Dispatch shows today's visits and what nobody owns yet.

More in the Scheduling guide and the Dispatch and On-call guide.

Your day

Calendar and your profile

TechniciansManagers
  1. Open My profile from your name.
  2. Press Make a feed address and copy it.
  3. Add it to your phone's calendar. It names tickets and places, never what a ticket says.
Your day

Time and timesheets

TechniciansManagers
  1. On the ticket, add time: start and end, or hours, with the work role and type.
  2. On Timesheets, check the week and press Submit.
  3. Your approver approves it or rejects it with a reason.

Try the time calculator in the Time guide.

Reference

Questions people ask

Everyone
I cannot see a request my colleague raised.
PMC Requests shows each person only their own.
My request is urgent but shows P4.
Add a note saying what changed, or phone the desk; a technician can change the answers.
It was closed but is still broken.
Reply to the closing email: most boards reopen it.
A board is missing from my list.
Ask its administrator to add you on Members & roles.
Can I delete a ticket or a note?
No. Duplicates are merged, mistakes are corrected with a new note.
Reference

Words the desk uses

Everyone
BoardA queue of work for one team.
TicketOne request, numbered PMC-000123.
PriorityP1 to P4, from two questions. Never typed.
SLA clocksRespond, Resolution plan, Resolve, on the board's working hours.
Subtype › ItemWhat the ticket is about: Printer › Failure.
Discussion noteThe requester can read it.
Internal noteThe desk only.
Resolution noteHow it was fixed.
ConfigurationA machine the desk looks after.
Restricted boardMembers only; every read audited.
PageAn urgent call, repeated until answered.
BizBoxPMC's finance system; the desk reads a copy.
